_comment: BASELINE DESIGN PROFILE — copy to <demo-root>\gate.config.json and replace every <...> token. This file arms the design leg on RUN ONE, before any styling exists, so the first gate run measures presentability and not just liveness. Every value here is generic Swift; nothing is tuned to one demo. Keys prefixed with _ are notes and are ignored by the runner.
_arming_rule: Do NOT leave the design leg unconfigured until the re-skin pass. A leg that arms at re-skin time stamps SKIP for the whole first half of the build, which is how a raw deserialize with skeleton bands and horizontal overflow reaches a PASS verdict. Arm it now; it is SUPPOSED to FAIL on a raw deserialize.

storyline._note: Bare 'placeholder' is deliberately ABSENT here. This leg scans markup, and Swift emits legitimate HTML placeholder= attributes on search and quantity inputs. It IS present in design.placeholderRegex below, which scans rendered text where attribute values never appear.

design._viewports_note: A VIEWPORT IS NOT A DEVICE. Dynamicweb picks the header SERVER-SIDE by user-agent, so a 390x844 viewport driven with the default headless desktop UA renders a document no phone user ever receives. Four consecutive gate PASSes were measured against the wrong document that way, and a mobile header height was correctly fitted to it. `device` is spread as a Playwright descriptor (UA + isMobile + hasTouch + DPR) BEFORE the explicit geometry, so the geometry still wins. `expectMobileHeader` asserts the SERVED ARTEFACT (the offcanvas nav marker), not the setting that was asked for -- so if the server stops UA-sniffing, or a later edit drops the descriptor, the leg fails loudly instead of silently reverting to the desktop page.
design._maxBandHeightFraction_note: No single image band may exceed 85% of the viewport height. Raise it ONLY for a deliberate full-bleed hero, and record the reason here next to the number -- an unexplained raised threshold is indistinguishable from a weakened one.
design._sectionGapThreshold_note: Maximum dead vertical gap between consecutive sections, in px. Catches the whitespace bands a deleted paragraph leaves behind.
design.placeholderRegex: lorem ipsum|\bLorem\b|\bdolor sit amet\b|Phosfluorescently|Holisticly|Authoritatively|Dramatically|Objectively|Synergistically|Monotonectally|Enthusiastically|Compellingly|Intrinsicly|Proactively|Continually transform|vortals|e-enable|team building|evisculate|vis-a-vis|window-licker|brand terrorists|wireless paradigms|Celebrate the beauty of our planet|Nurturing nature|Imagine a world where nature thrives|Embrace the green|Join the movement for a greener tomorrow|Our planet is full of wonder|Embrace a greener tomorrow|The choices we make today shape the world|Celebrating nature|Together for a brighter future|Preserve today, enjoy tomorrow|Respect the Earth|Small changes, big impact|Whether it.s in our homes|Nature.s beauty is in the little things|Sophie Greene|How can I start living a more eco-friendly lifestyle|Begin by making small changes in your daily routine|Discover Nature|Explore the Outdoors|Experience the beauty of nature with our guided tours|Latest travel guides|Explore the World One Pedal at a Time|Share the fun|Swift Frontpage|\bTODO\b|sample[- ]?text|xxxx+|coming soon|\bplaceholder\b
design._placeholderRegex_note: THREE BANDS, kept separable so one false positive can be retired without weakening the rest. Band 1 -- the stock corporate-ipsum SENTENCE-OPENER VERBS. Filler is only sometimes the word 'lorem'; the verb signature is what is actually live on a stock PDP and FAQ. Band 2 -- the content item-type defaultValue copy and the stock page copy (the zero-state tripwire; see references/zero-state.md). Regenerate band 2 from the layer's itemtypes/*.xml defaultValue attributes when the layer version rolls, rather than maintaining it by hand. Note `Whether it.s` and `Nature.s`: the shipped strings use a typographic apostrophe (U+2019), so a pattern typed with a straight quote matches NOTHING. Band 3 -- generic filler. DELIBERATELY NOT INCLUDED: bare 'synergy' and bare 'paradigms', which occur in legitimate B2B marketing prose -- 'wireless paradigms' keeps the discriminating half. AN ASSERT THAT FIRES ON GOOD COPY IS A BROKEN ASSERT, NOT A STRICT ONE. If a band-2 alternative collides with this customer's real business (an environmental brand, a travel brand), retire that ONE alternative and record why here.
design._pages_note: Include a PDP and a category PLP from run one. Those are the two page types where escaped defects actually live -- stock product copy and PLP row-content gaps are invisible on the front page. Add every page the storyline lands on.

plp._rowSelector_note: The [data-product-id] qualifier is load-bearing. The Swift item repeater emits one TRAILING <article class="product"> template row with NO data-product-id; an unqualified selector counts it and reports one phantom product on an empty PLP.
plp._requiredFields_note: Row COUNT is not row CONTENT. A PLP can render the right number of cards with no thumbnail, no SKU and no price on any of them. These four are asserted per row.

p29._transport_note: This block rides inside design.plp.p29 because the gate wrapper forwards a FIXED key list to the runner (baseUrl / viewports / maxBandHeightFraction / sectionGapThreshold / placeholderRegex / pages / plp) and a new top-level block would be SILENTLY DROPPED -- a config that reads as armed and executes nothing. The runner reads `cfg.p29 ?? cfg.plp.p29`, so the block moves to top level unchanged the moment the wrapper forwards the whole design object.
p29._cookies_note: Pre-seed consent, or the site's cookie modal renders over every screenshot. This was found by actually LOOKING at the first screenshots a design leg had ever taken: every one of them was a full-screen picture of the consent dialog, and every assert underneath it had been measuring that dialog.
p29._clearance_note: gap = firstContent.top - header.bottom, at EVERY viewport and page. It asserts the RELATIONSHIP rather than a hand-fitted pixel value, so it is self-maintaining across a header redesign. A large positive value is the white band under a sticky header; a large negative one is content sliding beneath it.

contrast.selector: main a[href], main button, main .btn, main [class*="cta"]

p29._contrast_note: WCAG 2.1 AA, computed colour against the nearest ancestor with background alpha > 0.5. Resolve the EFFECTIVE alpha before treating a value as failing -- a translucent overlay changes the real ratio.

ctas.selector: main a[data-dw-button], main a.btn, main [class*='cta'] a
ctas._note: Assert POSITIVELY by selector and count: the CTA must EXIST and BE BUTTON-SHAPED. The anti-pattern this replaces is asserting the ABSENCE OF A STRING and reading it as the PRESENCE OF A BUTTON -- a check written that way passed while seven primary conversion CTAs were live at display:inline, 19px tall, transparent, contrast 1.14.

requiredSections._note: Presence AND rendered height. A collapsed display:none shell satisfies a presence-only check. Height is what catches a section that was silently deleted -- and a HEADING alone would survive deletion of the content beneath it, so measure the CONTENT element, not its label.

p29._docHeight_note: A COMPONENT's height is invisible to every other assert here. A single spec or BOM section rendering ~18 phone screens tall passed required-section, section-gap, text-overlap, overflowX and the CSSOM census simultaneously, because each of those asks whether a thing is PRESENT, ALIGNED or PARSED and none of them asks how TALL the page got.
p29._textOverlap_note: No two text rects may intersect by more than 25% of the smaller. Ancestor/descendant pairs excluded.

cssom._note: BYTES IN A FILE ARE NOT PROOF A RULE PARSED. A literal comment terminator inside comment prose closes a banner early and the parser error-recovers by eating the next real rule -- every byte-level check still sees a healthy sheet. Leave `markers` empty until the first styled block ships, then add ONE marker per shipped sentinel block, taken VERBATIM from the live CSSOM (matching is on whitespace-collapsed selectorText, so a one-character difference is a marker that can never be present). Prefer the declaration whose loss would be INVISIBLE -- one whose value a framework default would silently supply.

design-signoff._note: Taste stays human. This leg reports SKIP ('awaiting human sign-off') until the artifact exists, then PASS. A SKIP is stamped, never a FAIL -- it records 'taste not yet reviewed' without blocking the build. The keeper screenshots at both breakpoints are what the human signs off on.
